documents: Published paper (PDF): Huang et al. (2022), Decadal Cooling Events in the South Indian Ocean During the Argo Era, JGR Oceans 127, e2021JC017949

entry.evidence: the potential reasons for this cooling trend have not been clearly explained

steps.action: Take from prior studies the reported decadal cooling above the thermocline in the tropical SWIO during the warming slowdown, against strong SEIO warming.
steps.quote: [...] variability above the thermocline in the tropical SWIO displayed a decadal cooling trend

steps.action: Pose the aim: the spatial structure of decadal SIO temperature change, focused on SWIO versus SEIO upper-layer contrast and the 400-1,000 m intermediate layer.
steps.quote: The main objective of this study is to investigate the spatial structure of decadal temperature changes in the SIO.

steps.action: Assemble three gridded observational temperature datasets (EN4, BOA-Argo, IAP), the IPO index, ERA5 and JRA55 atmospheric reanalyses, and the ECCOv4r4 ocean state estimate; apply anomalies, an 8-year Lanczos low-pass filter and a Mann-Kendall test.
steps.quote: The observational temperature datasets used in this study were derived from three ocean gridded temperature datasets

steps.action: Run EOF analysis of low-pass-filtered 0-300 m IAP temperature: EOF-1 is subtropical warming and EOF-2 is an east-west dipole with SWIO cooling periods 1992-2000 and 2005-2011.
steps.quote: Empirical Orthogonal Function (EOF) analysis was performed on the 8-year low-pass-filtered upper layer (0–300 m) temperature

steps.action: Check the ECCO reanalysis premise by repeating the EOF on ECCO and comparing its patterns and PCs with IAP.
steps.quote: thus validating the accuracy of ECCO in reproducing the observed decadal variability in the SIO

steps.action: Map 2005-2011 upper-300 m temperature trends in EN4, IAP, Argo and ECCO, establishing significant SWIO cooling (10-20°S, 60-90°E) across products.
steps.quote: all the four products exhibit similar spatial patterns of temperature trends despite some discrepancies in amplitudes

steps.action: Correlate regional-mean SWIO upper-layer decadal temperature with the IPO index (r = 0.92 for IAP).
steps.quote: the correlation coefficient between the IAP data set and the IPO index reaches 0.92 during 1992–2017

steps.action: Estimate 2005-2011 linear trends per product (-0.37 to -0.59 °C/decade) and diagnose the ECCO upper-300 m heat budget: anticorrelated air-sea flux and advection terms, with flux dominating 2005-2008 and advection dominating 2009-2011.
steps.quote: a heat budget analysis based on ECCO reanalysis was performed for the upper 300 m temperature in the tropical SWIO

steps.action: Check ECCO surface heat fluxes against JRA55, and latent heat anomalies against ERA5 and JRA55, finding consistent signs and patterns with amplitude differences.
steps.quote: The JRA55 reanalysis data set was used to validate surface heat fluxes of ECCO.

steps.action: Decompose latent heat flux anomalies with the bulk formula into wind-speed, humidity-gradient and nonlinear terms, attributing latent heat changes mainly to trade-wind speed variability.
steps.quote: sea surface wind variability plays a dominant role in determining changes in latent heat flux during 2005–2011

steps.action: Invoke the published mechanism that wind stress curl changes drive sea level change and meridional migration of tropical-subtropical gyre boundaries.
steps.quote: changes in wind stress curl in tropical oceans can also result in sea level fluctuations and the corresponding meridional migrations of the tropical-subtropical gyre boundaries

steps.action: Diagnose wind stress curl, SEC axis, SSH isoline and meridional advection in ECCO: the northward gyre expansion warms in 2005-2008, and the southward tropical-gyre expansion cuts meridional heat advection by 67% in 2009-2011.
steps.quote: this southward expansion (contraction) of the tropical (subtropical) gyre induced a 67% decrease in

steps.action: Keep the claim that the 2005-2011 SWIO cooling results from competing air-sea heat flux and ocean heat advection, both tied to low-level atmospheric circulation.
steps.quote: [...] event in the tropical SWIO during 2005–2011 is a result of the competing effect between air-sea heat flux and ocean heat advection

steps.action: Pose the second question: decadal variability in the 400-1,000 m intermediate layer, previously unclear.
steps.quote: however, the decadal variability in the intermediate layer (400–1,000 m) is unclear

steps.action: Run EOF analysis of 400-1,000 m temperature independently in IAP and ECCO; EOF-1 (~29%) shows basin-wide subtropical variability, and the PCs disagree before 2010 but agree on cooling in 2010-2016.
steps.quote: the EOF analysis was performed independently for the 400–1,000 m mean temperature in the IAP data set and the ECCO simulation

steps.action: Estimate 2010-2016 intermediate-layer linear trends from EN4, IAP and Argo (-0.24, -0.18, -0.28 °C/decade).
steps.quote: All the three observational datasets show a consistent cooling trend from 2010 to 2016.

steps.action: Compare ECCO with observations in the intermediate layer: ECCO shows biases before 2010 (an abnormal 2006-2009 warming) and better agreement after 2010.
steps.quote: Obvious model biases also extend to the period 2006–2009

steps.action: Restrict the intermediate-layer process analysis to 2010-2016, where ECCO and observations agree, after the pre-2010 mismatch.
steps.quote: we only investigated the physical processes during the consistent cooling period of 2010–2016

steps.action: Map 2010-2016 400-1,000 m trends and zonal-mean transects in four products, showing significant, vertically uniform cooling at 17-30°S.
steps.quote: At depths of 400–1,000 m, there exist vertically uniform and significant cooling trends.

steps.action: Diagnose the ECCO 400-1,000 m heat budget and decompose vertical advection into mean and anomaly terms: vertical advection dominates, driven by anomalous vertical velocity w'.
steps.quote: the negative vertical advection (−0.030°C/yr) made a dominant contribution to the cooling trend (−0.0228°C/yr) during 2010–2016

steps.action: Check the w' attribution against the upward shift of isotherms seen in the observational datasets and in ECCO.
steps.quote: is also supported by the upward shift of isotherms during 2010–2016 in the observation datasets and ECCO

steps.action: Quantify the SWIO cooling's effect on basin-mean SIO warming in 2005-2011 (0.43 to 0.28 °C/decade, a 35% reduction).
steps.quote: After including this cooling signal, the average warming rate in the SIO decreased from 0.43°C/decade to 0.28°C/decade during 2005–2011.

steps.action: Keep the claim that vertical advection from anomalous upward velocity dominates the 2010-2016 intermediate-layer cooling.
steps.quote: Results reveal that vertical advection plays a dominant role in decadal cooling in the 400–1,000 m layer of the subtropical SIO.

steps.action: Contrast the out-of-phase upper and intermediate SIO tendencies with the vertically uniform South Pacific variability reported by Volkov et al. (2017).
steps.quote: This feature is different from the case of the SPO where the interannual-to-decadal OHC variability are predominantly vertically uniform

tree.answer: Two decadal cooling events inside a warming SIO (upper SWIO 2005-2011; subtropical intermediate layer 2010-2016)
Temperature is observed in gridded datasets; heat budget terms are not observed and are diagnosed from ECCO
Explain the causes of the cooling by heat budget attribution
No stated rivals; candidate budget terms (air-sea flux, horizontal and vertical advection, diffusion) are compared
No distinct predictions derived for rivals
Conditions found in nature (specific decadal periods), not set
Cooling repeats across EN4, IAP, Argo and ECCO; ECCO fluxes checked against JRA55 and ERA5; ECCO fails in the intermediate layer before 2010, so the analysis is restricted
Mechanism attributions kept as budget estimates
Four anonymous reviewers acknowledged; no review file supplied

end.claim: Two decadal cooling events occurred in the SIO during the Argo era: upper-300 m SWIO cooling in 2005-2011 (-0.50 ± 0.1 °C/decade), from competing air-sea heat flux and horizontal advection; and 400-1,000 m subtropical cooling in 2010-2016, dominated by vertical advection from anomalous upward velocity.

decisive_move.sentence: The ECCO heat budget diagnoses for the upper-300 m SWIO and the 400-1,000 m subtropical layer, with their term decompositions, produce the mechanism claims; without them only the observed cooling would remain.

gates.evidence: All data are existing gridded products and reanalyses chosen for a descriptive aim; no hypothesis directed data acquisition. The cooling itself faced cross-dataset checks it could have failed (p. 5-6, 11). The intermediate-layer reanalysis check did fail before 2010, leading to restriction to 2010-2016 (p. 11). The w' attribution was checked against observed isotherm shifts (p. 13). The budget attributions rest on a single closed-budget product (ECCO) and faced no rival test. Nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Mann-Kendall trend significance test (modified for autocorrelation, Hamed & Rao 1998)

novelty_claims.quote: Similar cooling patterns were reported in several previous studies (e.g., Li, Han, & Zhang, 2017; Liao et al., 2019), but the relevant causes have not [...]
in addition to the oceanic process, sea surface heat exchange is also crucial for shaping the decadal changes of SWIO thermal structure

limits: No peer-review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded, although the acknowledgments mention four reviewers. The paper makes no explicit 'first' claims; the novelty entries are 'not explained' and 'also crucial' statements. Composition is none_fits: the walk is a diagnostic attribution study. A question leads to cross-dataset establishment of the phenomenon and then budget diagnosis in one reanalysis, with no stated rivals or crucial test, so it is neither strong_inference nor trace_series (which needs stated rivals). Sub-claims: the existence of both cooling events (replicated across EN4, IAP, Argo and ECCO) is effectively confirmed as a pattern; the upper-layer mechanism (latent heat flux versus gyre-driven advection) is closer to best_explanation, as it rests on ECCO budgets with flux checks against JRA55 and ERA5; the intermediate-layer w' attribution is an estimate restricted to 2010-2016, where ECCO agrees with observations, and its cause is left for future study (p. 14). The budget is in fixed-depth Cartesian coordinates, and the authors note that isopycnal and Subantarctic Mode Water processes may contribute (p. 14). The authors cannot tell whether pre-2010 discrepancies come from sparse observations or model dynamics (p. 15). Inference: the 2005-2011 and 2010-2016 windows appear to have been chosen after inspecting the PCs and time series, not fixed in advance. Budget-term uncertainties are given only as standard deviations (error bars).

disagreements.target: Li et al. (2018); Zhang et al. (2018): SIO warming during 1998-2015 attributed to enhanced ITF heat transport
disagreements.support: The paper argues the 1998 start reflects yearly means contaminated by the 1997-1998 El Niño; low-pass-filtered decadal signals show warming beginning in 1993.
disagreements.quote: Note that the results in these previous studies were based on the yearly mean temperature

disagreements.target: Existing studies (Jin et al., 2018; Schwarzkopf & Böning, 2011) emphasizing oceanic waves and circulation adjustment for SWIO decadal variability
disagreements.support: The ECCO heat budget shows air-sea (latent) heat flux is of similar amplitude to, and anticorrelated with, ocean heat advection (r = -0.83).
disagreements.quote: Existing studies have mainly focused on the dominant contribution of oceanic waves and circulation adjustment to the decadal temperature variability in the [...]

disagreements.target: Volkov et al. (2017): vertically uniform interannual-to-decadal OHC variability in the South Pacific
disagreements.support: The SIO upper and intermediate layers are out of phase in 2010-2013 and in phase in 2014-2016, unlike the SPO case.
disagreements.quote: This feature is different from the case of the SPO where the interannual-to-decadal OHC variability are predominantly vertically uniform
